chunks: From him, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, from ʿAlī, peace be upon him.
That the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, used to detain in a blood accusation for six days; then if the heirs of the slain came with proof, otherwise he would let him go.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ: the legal heirs or claimants of the slain
key_terms.بِبَيِّنَةٍ: with clear legal proof or evidence
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُ: released him and let him go free

ai.seo_question: How long could a person be detained in a blood accusation if the heirs had not yet produced evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله concerning a person accused in a blood case. The accused would be detained for six days pending proof from the heirs of the slain, and if no evidence was produced, he would be released.
